rationale: Both use gradient x mean-shift decomposition and true-logit synthetic notes, but A flips all style properties at fixed topic (dep threshold for none) while B uses topic-vs-style conflict notes and inspection of shares; A uses pooled gender x case 4-cell effect vectors, B cross-probe sign-pattern cosine; B verifies by ablation, A does not; regex checks differ.

Shared decomposition and corpus-example labelling. A uses one all-properties-flipped pair per probe and dep=d_prop/(gap-d_prop); B uses single-property flip triples (case, gender) with ratio<0.3 rule. A picks latents via pooled 4-cell gender/case effects; B via cross-probe same-sign shift. B adds ablation check; A submits two cues, B one.

A assigns latents by hand labels plus 4-cell gender x case effects, estimates dependence from one bundle-flip pair; B assigns latents to property buckets by z-scored cross-probe sign fingerprints with balance filter, uses SEM, single-property true-logit spot checks, bucket ratio>=0.3 rule, ablation check, and vocab/closing completeness scans.
